Rh-Catalyzed Kinetic Resolution-Based Enantioselective  
[4+2]-Cycloaddition-Isomerization of Allene-1,3-dienes 
Anni Qin,a Qian Zhang,a Hui Qian,*,a Yulin Han,*,a and Shengming Ma*,a,b 
a Research Center for Molecular Recognition and Synthesis, Department of Chemistry, Fudan University, 220 Handan Lu, Shanghai 200433,

The first example of Rh-catalyzed kinetic resolution of 1,3-disubstituted allene-1,3-dienes involving intramolecular [4+2]-cycloaddition 
has been developed. Followed by C=C isomerization, the reaction finally afforded aza -[4.3.0]bicyclic compounds with a very high  en-
antio- and E-selectivity. The mechanism has been unveiled by careful control experiments. The synthetic potentials of highly  enanti-
oenriched bicyclic products have also been demonstrated.

Background and Originality Content 
Aza-[4.3.0]bicyclic structure is a core motif of many biologi -
cally active compounds: for example, captan[1a] and captafol[1b] are 
common agrochemicals for sterilization; serlopitant, [1c] miti-
glinide,[1d] and its derivatives have bioactivities fo r the treatment 
of prurigo nodulari and type 2 diabetes, respectively (Scheme 1a). 
Intramolecular [4+2] -cycloadditions between 1,3 -dienes and al -
kenes or alkynes are among the most powerful tools for the con -
struction of such bicyclic functionalized compou nds.[2-4] Intramo-
lecular [4+2]-cycloadditions between 1,3 -dienes and allenes may 
also afford aza -[4.3.0]bicyclic products with extra handle for syn-
thetic elaboration.[5] However, there is an issue of axial chirality in 
the allenes as compared to alkenes and alkynes, and such enanti-
oselective reaction with axially chiral allenes has never been es -
tablished. Challenges are the recognition of the axial  chirality in 
the starting materials and the enantioselectivity as well as the 
Z/E-selectivity for the remaining C=C bond. There are reports on 
synthesis of such optically active bicyclic products from optically 
active substrates based on chirality transfer (Scheme 1b -i).[7] We 
wish to report the first example of Rh -catalyzed sequential [4+2] 
cycloaddition/C=C bond isomerization of racemic allene-dienes, in 
which both kinetic resolution of the axially chiral substrate s and 
enantioselective cycloaddition were achieved to afford aza-[4.3.0]-
bicyclic compounds in high enantioselectivity (Scheme 1b-ii).

Results and Discussion 
Our initial studies began with the [4+2] -cycloaddition of race-
mic allene -diene (2 E,4E)-1a under the catalysis of [Rh(coe) 2Cl]2 
and AgSbF6 with different chiral ligands in EtOH at 60 °C (Table 1). 
(R,R)-Norphos [(2R,3R)-(–)-2,3-bis(diphenylphosphino)-bicyclo-
[2.2.1]hept-5-ene] L1 was initially employed as the chiral ligand, 
and normal [4+2] -cycloaddition product 2a[7b] was formed in 59% 
yield with 42% ee with no starting material remained ( entry 1). 
(R,R)-Me-DUPHOS (1,2-bis[(2R,5R)-2,5-dimethyl-1-phospholanyl]-
benzene) L2 slightly improved the yield to 64% and ee to 56%. 
Ferrocene-based phosphine ligand ( L3) failed to afford 2a and 
(S)-p-Tol-BINAP [(S)-2.2'-Bis(di-p-tolylphosphino)-1,1'-binaphthyl] 
L4 was also inefficient for this reaction ( entries 3 and 4). Menthol 
derived ligand L5 and Feringa ligand L6 were also efficient in pro-
ducing the product 2a, however, the enantioselectivity is very low 
(entries 5 and 6). Surprisingly, when (R,R)-Ph-BPE {1,2-bis[(2R,5R)- 
2,5-diphenylphospholan-1-yl]ethane} L7 was used as the ligand, 
we did not observe the formation of normal [4+2]-cycloaddition 
product 2a. Instead, the sequential [4+2] -cycloaddition and C=C 
bond isomerization product 3a was obtained in 29% yield with 95% 
ee. Instead of recovering starting material, 47 % NMR yield of 
tetra-ene (2E,4E,9Z,11E)-1a' was also observed (entry 7).

After identifying ( R,R)-Ph-BPE as the best ligand, other reac -
tion parameters were examined (Table 2). Firstly, we found the 
catalyst loading could be reduced to 2.5 mol% without losing the 
efficiency for the transformation ( entry 1). Next, various silver 
salts were screened, and AgSbF 6 was found to be optimal ( entries 
2—4), which revealed that anions have an effect on the reaction. 
n-PrOH was inappropriate, resulting in 18% of 3a albeit with 98%

toluene with 70 %—74% recovery of 1a (entries 6 and 7). No  de-
sired product 3a was observed with  [Rh(nbd)Cl]2 as the catalyst 
(entry 8). When [Rh(C 2H4)2Cl]2 was used, the yield of 3a was im-
proved to 36% with an excellent enantioselectivity while the yield 
of (2E,4E,9Z,11E)-1a' was 52% ( entry 9). Thus, optimal conditions 
for the molecular recognition have been defined as 2.5 mol% of 
[Rh(C2H4)2Cl]2, 5 mol% of ( R,R)-Ph-BPE, and 5 mol% of AgSbF 6 in 
EtOH at 45 °C. 
With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, the scope of 
the Rh-catalyzed intramolecular [4+2] -cycloaddition-C=C bond 
isomerization of allene-dienes was investigated (Table 3). Both R 1 
and R3 may be H or an alkyl group (entries 1 —14). This protocol is 
very general for the R 2 group including 1°-alkyl ranging from C 1 to 
C10 (entries 1—10) and 2°-alkyl group (entry 12). A free hydroxyl 
group in R 2 could also be well tolerated (entry 13). The absolute 
configuration of 3k was established by the X -ray single crystal 
diffraction study (Figure 1). Since there is no method  for the syn-
thesis of the racemic products to determine the ee of the optically 
active products, ( S,S)-Ph-BPE was used as the ligand to produce 
the enantiomers of corresponding prod ucts with a similar effi -
ciency (right column, Table 3). 
 
Figure 1  ORTEP representation of (3aS,7aS,E)-3k. 
To gain insight into the mechanism of isomerization process, 
the normal [4+2] -cycloaddition product (3a S,5R,7aS,Z)-2a was 
prepared according to the known protocol. [7b] No reaction oc -
curred in the absence of the ligand (Scheme 2a, left) while the 
same C=C isomerization product (3aS,7aS,E)-3a was formed in the 
presence of ( R,R)-Ph-BPE or ( S,S)-Ph-BPE (Scheme 2a, right).  Fur-
thermore, when the racemic normal [4+2] -cycloaddition product 
(3aR*,5S*,7aR*,Z)-2a was subjected to the standard conditions,  
Table 3  Scope study 
 
88% of the C=C bond isomerized product (3a S,7aS,E)-3a was ob-
tained with an enantioselectivity of only 8% (Scheme 2b). It clear -
ly revealed that (3aS,5R,7aS,Z)-2a was formed via enantioselective 
[4+2]-cycloaddition first, which was followed by C=C bond isom -
erization to afford the final product (3aS,7aS,E)-3a. Such C=C bond 
isomerization may be catalyzed by the in situ generated Rh-H spe-
cies, which was supported by the fact that only the normal 
[4+2]-cycloaddition product (3a S,5R,7aS,Z)-2a was generated in a 
low ee together with the formation of (2 E,4E,9Z,11E)-1a' when 
running the reaction in aprotic solvent such as  THF (tetrahydrofu-
ran) and DCM (dichloromethane) due to the lack of Rh -H species 
(Scheme 2c, entries 1 & 2). No reaction was observed in MeCN or 
dioxane (Scheme 2c, entries 3 & 4). To know more about the 
mechanism, the reaction of (2 E,4E)-1a under the standard condi -
tions was monitored by 1H NMR and HPLC  analysis (Scheme 2d) 
and the ees of normal [4+2] -cycloaddition product (3aS,5R,7aS,Z)- 
2a and (3a S,7aS,E)-3a kept constant while the ee of recovered 
(Sa,2E,4E)-1a increased, indicating that the normal [4+2] -cyclo-
addition product (3a S,5 R,7a S,Z)-2a would i somerize to 
(3aS,7aS,E)-3a during the reaction. We also prepared both enan -
tiomers of 1a via EATA (enantioselective allenation of terminal 
alkynes)[8] and submitted them to the standard conditions, re -
spectively: (3aS,7aS,E)-3a was obtained from ( Sa,2E,4E)-1a in 61% 
yield with >99% ee accompanied with 30% yield of 
(2E,4E,9Z,11E)-1a'; when ( Ra,2E,4E)-1a was applied, (2 E,4E,9Z,- 
11E)-1a' was formed exclusively in 84% isolated yield (Scheme 2e). 
These results supported that the reaction  involves a parallel ki -
netic resolution process. When ( Ra,2E,4E)-1a or (Sa,2E,4E)-1a was 
subjected to the standard conditions with EtOH -d6 as solvent, the 
incorporation of the deuterium atom in product (2 E,4E,9Z,11E)- 
1a'' was not observed, indicating that the isomerization of allene-

allene‐diene  (2E,4E)‐1o  and  oxygen‐tethered  (2E,4E)‐1p  failed  to

Based on these studies, a possible mechanism is proposed as 
shown in Scheme 3. Firstly, [Rh(C2H4)2Cl]2 reacted with AgSbF6 and 
chiral ligand (L*) to generate chiral cationic catalyst [RhL*]+, which 
preferred to react with (Sa,2E,4E)‐1 to form the intermediate A via 
ligand exchange when the chiral ligand was (R,R)‐Ph‐BPE (path a). 
Subsequent  cyclometalation  afforded  intermediate  B,  which 
would lead to the formation of rhodiabicycloheptene C via allyl‐Rh 
isomerization.  Subsequent  reductive  elimination  yielded  the  nor‐
mal  [4+2]‐cycloaddition  pr oduct  (3aS,5R,7aS,Z)‐2  with  the  regen‐
eration  of  the  catalytically  active  [RhL*]+  species.  The  in  situ 
formed Rh hydride species catalyzed the C=C bond isomerization 
to afford the final product (3aS,7aS,E)‐3 via sequential hydromet‐
alation  and β ‐H  elimination.  (Sa,2E,4E)‐1  may  also  slowly  coordi‐
nate  with  [RhL*]+  species  and  subsequent  oxidative  addition 
would afford an allyl‐Rh‐hydride intermediate E, which could yield 
the product (2E,4E,9Z,11E)‐1' after reductive elimination and dis‐
sociation.[9]  According  to  the  results  shown  in  Scheme  2e, 
(Ra,2E,4E)‐1 isomerized exclusively to (2E,4E,9Z,11E)‐1' via path b 
with (R,R)‐Ph‐BPE as the chiral ligand. 
The highly functionalized nature of the products makes them 
very useful in organic synthesis: The reaction of (3aS,7aS,E)‐3 with 
mCPBA  (3‐chlor operoxybenzoic   acid)  afforded  the  double  epoxi‐
dation  product  4  with  an  excellent  diastereoselectivity  (Scheme 
4a).  The  absolute  configurations  of  the  chiral  centers  in  4  were 
established via its X‐ray diffraction study. In the presence of OsO4, 
(3aS,7aS,E)‐3a  may  be  converted  to  regioisomeric  dihydroxylated 
products  5a  and  6a.  The  oxidation  of  6a  in  this  mixture  with 
Dess‐Martin  periodinane  afforded α ‐hydroxyl  ketone  7a  with  the 
5a unreacted (Scheme 4b, up). In addition, when the dihydroxyla‐
tion  mixture  was  treated  with  10  mol%  of  Ts OH   in  acetone,  the 
diol  in  5a  could  be  protected  highly  selectively  by  its  treatment 
with  acetone  to  afford  the  corresponding  ketal  8a  while  6a  was 
converted  to  the α,β‐unsaturated ketone  9a  (Scheme  4b,  down).

Conclusions 
In  conclusion,  we  have  developed  the  [Rh(C2H4)2Cl]2/AgSbF6‐ 
cocatalyzed  kinetic  resolution‐based  [4+2]‐cycloaddition  of  race‐
mic  1,3‐disubstituted  allene‐dienes,  which  was  followed  by  an 
exclusive cyclic C=C bond isomerization to afford cis‐[4.3.0]bicyclic 
products  with  an  excellent  enantio‐  and  E‐selectivity  while  the 
allene unit in the (R)‐enantiomer has been converted to a conju‐
gated  1,3‐dien e  with  (R,R)‐Ph‐BPE  as  the  ligand.  The  bicyclic 
products  have  been  easily  transformed  to  other  useful  optically 
active  highly  functionalized  cis‐fused  bicyclic  molecules.  The  na‐
ture of the kinetic resolution process has been carefully unveiled.
